# Whether a point is a member of an interval, two-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_contains_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Whether the point $t = t_0 + t_1$ is a finite number and a member of $X$, $X = [x_l, x_u]$; a mask that is true only if it holds:

$$m \implies t = t_0 + t_1 \in X.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x_l = x_{l0} + x_{l1}$, $x_u = x_{u0} + x_{u1}$, $t = t_0 + t_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X.contains(t)` | `Interval<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | `bool` | `constexpr`; does not round |
| `X.contains(t)` | `Interval<T, 2>`, `T` | `bool` | the point made a number of two limbs by `make_2` first, exactly: a composition of two proved kernels, not machine-checked as one statement; `constexpr`; does not round |
| `member(t, X)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Interval<T, 2>` | `Trit` | as a `Trit`: yes or no, never unknown; `constexpr`; does not round |
| `member(t, X)` | `T`, `Interval<T, 2>` | `Trit` | as a `Trit`: yes or no, never unknown; the point made a number of two limbs by `make_2` first, exactly: a composition of two proved kernels, not machine-checked as one statement; `constexpr`; does not round |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X = [x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.
- $t$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $m$ is true exactly when the point $t = t_0 + t_1$ is a finite number and a member of $X$: the answer is exact.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_contains_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalPredicates.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalPredicates.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_contains_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_contains_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the bounds compared with the point by le_2_2, and a test that the point is finite (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_contains_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_contains_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`le_2_2`](le_2_2.md).

```
# Whether a 2-limb value t is a member of an interval with 2-limb bounds (milestone2.md, "One
# enclosure interface", the row of contains(t)): x_l <= t and t <= x_u by le_2_2, which is exact on
# canonical values, and t finite (its leading limb). As for one limb, an infinite t is no member, a
# NaN fails every comparison and the empty set has no member. Exact. For every precision.

a  = le_2_2(xl0, xl1, t0, t1)
b  = le_2_2(t0, t1, xu0, xu1)
ta = abs(t0)
ft = lt(ta, const inf)
ab = and(a, b)
m  = and(ab, ft)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#interval_contains_2)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 4 domains of 4 formats | 18 916 496 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
